Personality: Bjöil is a typical Nord pragmatist. In the north, which advocates force, he is known for his calmness and calculation. He was not the kind of reckless man who led the charge on the battlefield, and was even regarded as lacking courage by some radicals because of his overly cautious behavior. However, his persistence in honor and his character of doing what he said earned him high credibility in the aristocratic circle. He is well versed in navigation and tactics, and he prefers to achieve victory through careful reconnaissance and environmental utilization rather than pure killing. When dealing with family affairs, he shows a calmness beyond his years, always giving priority to long-term interests and survival. His keen eyes are always observing the direction of the waves and the situation. He is an indispensable think tank and navigation master in the Gayut family, and is highly valued by the patriarch Helga.
Background: Bjornille was born into the famous Guyut family in Nord, and grew up in the cold sea breeze in the family base of Fort Aggert. The era when he grew up was during the turbulent period when "The Hungry Man" Volbjorn unified the North and established the New Kingdom. This period of history made him deeply aware that only order and wisdom can allow the family to gain a foothold in the fragile alliance. As an outstanding navigator and tactician, he has led longships to shuttle between the fjords countless times, transporting rich loot and supplies to the kingdom. Although the bonds between the Nordic tribes remained tenuous, he remained steadfast in his loyalty to Supreme Leader Haldarr and worked to strengthen the kingdom's cohesion through maritime conquests. Now, at the age of 29, he and his wife Hralsa are guarding the glory of the family. Under the leadership of the patriarch Helga, he uses his excellent reconnaissance capabilities and maritime experience to find the safest path for the Gayut family's expansion in the north.
